newsitem.title: USA: ADM, units targeted in European probe.
newsitem.headline: ADM, units targeted in European probe.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co., which pleaded guilty to price-fixing charges in the U.S. last year, is now the target of a similar probe in Europe, the company said Wednesday.
ADM and several of its European subsidiaries are among the subjects of an anti-competitive practices investigation by the Commission of the European Communities, the company said.

ADM, the huge agricultural products processor, said in a statement the commission is probing the possible participation of major manufacturers in anticompetitive practices or agreements in certain markets for amino acids, including the feed additive lysine, in the European Union.
ADM pleaded guilty in the U.S. last year to fixing prices of lysine and the food additive citric acid, and paid a record $100 million in fines.
The U.S. Justice Department probe also resulted in charges against Ajinomoto Co. Inc. and Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co. Ltd. of Japan and Sewon America Inc..
ADM said the European probe was in its early stages and the outcome could not be predicted.
